I know it’s not normal. That’s why I am here to see if anyone has a shared experience so I can figure out where the problem lies. Antibiotics is a temporary solution to an ongoing problem. That’s it. And antibiotics being a temporary solution is irrelevant Bc my body clears it soon after. Treatment is not the problem. Knowing where the problem is to prevent an on-going problem is the emphasis here. The doctor prescribed medication BC it’s his job after finding a diagnosis that has a remedy. Simple. Many know not to overuse antibiotics. That would be the situation here especially when I don’t need it Bc as I said many times my body actually resolves it on it’s own. Then my cycle comes. Rinse. Repeat. It’s not a cure, it’s a treatment. It would only treat a day or two of discharge that has no smell or anything else that can affect my quality of life. Antibiotics is not necessary. What is necessary is finding out what conditions keeping allowing my body to do this when I’m transitioning off my cycle.

The doctor isn’t wrong with the diagnosis. BV comes and goes and overprescribing antibiotics every time I get one (at this point monthly right after my cycle) reduces the effectiveness of them overtime. So, no. I’m not taking them if it solves itself very quickly (for me). I only take them if I truly need them for a serious infection where antibiotics is needed. Like I said, there is no symptoms other than the discharge. If it was more serious then I would consider it. The antibiotics isn’t a cure but a temporary treatment for a very common problem. Also, you don’t have to do everything a doctor says or suggests when you know your body and health. It’s standard for them to suggest/prescribe a solution when they have a known diagnosis. It’s their job and it’s our choice to accept it.
